reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for four fixes. Claude Code command approval: the Claude Code reference now says the session's permission mode is learned from its hooks, the mode it was started with, or permissions.defaultMode, and is Claude Code's default when none names one, so first-time setup inside Claude Code offers and writes the rules on the User's yes; when setup cannot add them it says why in one line, which the agent relays without retrying. Project identity: a submodule or nested checkout under a repository with .notifai/config.toml now belongs to that repository's Project for name, config and enablement, and the home folder is never a Project, so --project writes there are refused with a plain message. Doctor's Codex hook trust line and the matching ask refusal now give one line per hooks file with a handler count and one action; the per-handler list is technical detail. Harness session markers count only when the caller runs inside that session's process tree, so a shell that merely inherited them is markerless. Readiness ids, hook output and the protocol are unchanged. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for three hub corrections: a SessionEnd the hub answered late is now decided by the hub alone (so a conversation its app or machine only stopped stays open, as the guidance already says), Linux names a process by its boot and kernel start ticks so a clock step no longer reads live sessions as gone, and the hub takes its proxy and certificate settings from the sign-in record (written once by the first hub starter on a machine signed in before there was one) while each session carries its own PATH and desktop. No agent-facing behaviour, command, flag or wording changed.
